audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Swain, Skill, Yone, Yone, Swain, Yone, Yone, which does not match the already-audited Swain side.
audit.why: mirrorFindings point 2 records rows 0 flipped to Yone and rows 2 and 5 flipped to Skill, as matched win[]/phases[].side pairs. Applied to the same starting chart this page carries, that gives Yone, Skill, Skill, Yone, Swain, Skill, Yone. The kit supports it: at level 1 Swain has one spell, no root and no Soul Fragments, so Yone's Q pressure wins; level 3 is even once Vision of Empire and Nevermove are both up; and first item is even because his drain answers your damage until Grievous Wounds is on.
audit.corrected: Set both layers to Yone, Skill, Skill, Yone, Swain, Skill, Yone.

audit.whatIsWrong: No numbers on any spike, and 'first item flips the lane' ignores what he buys.
audit.why: Nevermove is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s and gets shorter during Demonic Ascension. Vision of Empire is 22s at rank 1 with 5500-7500 range. Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s. Ravenous Flock turns every Soul Fragment into healing plus a permanent maximum-health increase, so his effective tankiness rises across the lane rather than at an item timing.
audit.corrected: Write 12s on Nevermove, 22s on Vision of Empire and the flat 120s on Demonic Ascension, and tie the first-item row to Grievous Wounds rather than to raw damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three mechanics are wrong or absent: the page says to 'wait out' Demonic Ascension and punish 'the deflated form', it never says when Nevermove roots, and it never says what Vision of Empire does for him.
audit.why: Riot's R text: 'This form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions.' It does not time out while you stand in it — breaking contact is what ends it, and waiting inside the drain is exactly how the ultimate is sustained. Riot's E text: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits' — the root is on the return trip, so a player who sidesteps the outgoing wave and then stands still gets rooted anyway, and he can pull rooted champions closer afterwards. Riot's W text: champions hit 'grant Swain a Soul Fragment', which the passive converts into healing and permanent maximum health — every W you eat makes him permanently tankier.
audit.corrected: Break away to end Demonic Ascension rather than waiting it out; dodge Nevermove's return, not its cast; and treat Vision of Empire as free permanent health for him.

audit.why: Executioner's Calling early is correct and the missingInteractions needs-antiheal entry agrees; the only refinement is that it should be online before the level-6 all-in, not merely 'early'.

edits.before: W shield-grit covers every exchange you start. Only take the trade when Swain's Demonic Ascension is down.
edits.after: Even at 2. Nevermove roots on the way back, not the way out — sidestep the return and the trade is yours.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Swain must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Vision of Empire is 22s and hands him a Soul Fragment on hit — every one you eat makes him permanently tankier.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Swain's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension lasts as long as he keeps draining a champion. Walking out ends it, standing there feeds it. 120s flat.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Demonic Ascension's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King lands, but so does his drain — get Grievous Wounds on before the all-in maths work.

edits.before: Swain owns L1 — ranged Q and E-root threat zone you off farm.
edits.after: L1 is yours — one spell, no root, and no Soul Fragments yet.

edits.before: At L2 his poke and root pressure keep you on the defensive.
edits.after: At L2 it's even: his Q chip against your Q3 knockup threat.

edits.before: Through 4-5 it stays a skill test around dodging his E root.
edits.after: Through 4-5 you win short trades whenever Nevermove misses.

edits.before: On first item you out-DPS his tanky build and take over.
edits.after: First item evens out: your DPS against his drain and heals.

edits.before: Swain R (Demonic Ascension) gives him huge sustain and burst in a fight; don't all-in into an active ult — wait it out, then punish the deflated form.
edits.after: Swain R (Demonic Ascension) drains everyone nearby and lasts as long as he keeps draining a champion — breaking away is what ends it, not waiting. 120s flat.

edits.before: Late you hard-scale past Swain — dodge his E (Nevermove) with your dash, deny the root that lands his whole combo, and shred him before Demonic Ascension stabilizes.
edits.after: Late you hard-scale past Swain — Nevermove (E) roots on its return trip, so sidestep the wave coming back, then shred him with Grievous Wounds already on before he drains.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 even out into a skill test: you can start dodging E and punishing his cooldown gaps, but his R at 6 makes all-ins risky. Bait the root, sidestep with E, and only commit when Nevermove is down and his ult isn't active.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 even out into a skill test: Nevermove roots on the return, not the cast, so sidestep the wave coming back and punish the 12-second gap. His R at 6 makes all-ins risky — commit only once the root is spent and your anti-heal is up.

edits.before: Zone you off CS with Q chip and W (Vision of Empire)
edits.after: Hit you with W for a Soul Fragment and permanent HP

notes: Best find, and the packet flagged nothing: the page tells the player to 'wait out' Demonic Ascension and punish 'the deflated form'. Riot's text says the form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions — standing in it to wait is what keeps it running. Second: Nevermove roots on the wave's RETURN, which the page never states, so 'dodge his E' was teaching the wrong dodge. Third: Vision of Empire grants a Soul Fragment, which Ravenous Flock turns into healing and permanent maximum health, so eating his W is not just chip. Chart follows mirrorFindings rather than packet.levelChart — the two disagree on rows 0, 1 and 3, and confidence on point 2 is Medium for that reason; see questionsForUser. Like the mirror agent, I did not touch the claims that Yone's Q3 deals true damage or that Spirit Cleave hits both damage types — neither is in Riot's text in the kit file.
